entry.statement: Suppose $(M,J)$ is an almost complex $4$-manifold with nonempty $\mathcal K_J^c$. Then $\mathcal K_J^t=\mathcal K_J^c+H_J^{(2,0),(0,2)}(M)_{\mathbb R}$. In particular, if $b^+(M)=1$, then $\mathcal K_J^t=\mathcal K_J^c$. Here $\mathcal K_J^t=\{[\omega]\in H^2(M;\mathbb R):\omega$ symplectic and tamed by $J\}$, $\mathcal K_J^c=\{[\omega]:\omega$ compatible with $J\}$, and $H_J^{(2,0),(0,2)}(M)_{\mathbb R}$ is the subspace of $H^2(M;\mathbb R)$ of classes represented by closed real $J$-anti-invariant 2-forms ($C^\infty$ version, Definition 2.1). It follows from Theorem 1.1 ($J$ $C^\infty$ full and $\mathcal K_J^c\ne\emptyset$ imply the same equality) and the fact (Draghici-Li-Zhang) that every almost complex structure on a 4-manifold is $C^\infty$ pure and full.

hypotheses.text: M is a closed oriented smooth manifold (paper-wide setting: closed oriented smooth 2n-manifold) and J an almost complex structure compatible with the orientation.
M has real dimension 4.
The J-compatible cone K_J^c is nonempty (J is almost Kaehler).
For the second assertion: b^+(M) = 1.

variables.bplus: b^+(M), the number of positive eigenvalues of the intersection form on H^2(M;R)

tameness.text: J tames omega if omega is positive on every J-line span(v,Jv), v nonzero (omega(v,Jv)>0); omega is J-compatible if it is tamed and J-invariant.

orientation.text: Symplectic forms are those compatible with the fixed orientation of M (omega^n a positive volume form), and J is compatible with the given orientation.

grading.text: H_J^{(2,0),(0,2)}(M)_R denotes de Rham classes of closed real J-anti-invariant 2-forms (forms, not currents, the 'C^infinity' groups); the current analogues use lower indices.

written.notes: Numbering: the published CAG version (read) labels this result Corollary 1.1 (separate counters per environment type); arXiv:0708.2520v4 has the same statement as Corollary 1.4 because there Definition 1.1, Question 1.2, Theorem 1.3 share the counter. The statement is identical in both versions.
written.typing_notes: tame_sign: sign of omega(v,Jv) required for J to tame omega (positive = omega(v,Jv)>0). compatible_requires: extra condition beyond tameness for compatibility (j_invariant = omega J-invariant). symplectic_orientation: whether omega^n agrees with the fixed orientation of M (matching/opposite). j_orientation: whether the orientation induced by J agrees with the fixed orientation (matching/opposite). anti_invariant_regularity: H_J^{(2,0),(0,2)} built from smooth forms (smooth) or currents (current). anti_invariant_reality: real or complex anti-invariant classes.

entry.statement: Let $Y$ be a contact manifold with contact form $\alpha$, $\xi=\ker\alpha$, and symplectization $(\mathbb R\times Y, d(e^s\alpha))$. Let $f_t\colon\Lambda\to Y$, $t\in[-1,1]$, be a self-transverse regular Legendrian homotopy, constant near its endpoints, connecting Legendrian embeddings $f_-$ and $f_+$, extended to all $t\in\mathbb R$ by $f_t=f_-$ for $t\le -1$ and $f_t=f_+$ for $t\ge 1$. Then there exists a self-transverse Lagrangian immersion $G\colon \mathbb R\times\Lambda\to\mathbb R\times Y$, $G(t,x)=(h(x,t),\tilde f_t(x))$, such that: (i) there is $T>0$ with $G(t,x)=(t,f_-(x))$ for $t<-T$ and $G(t,x)=(t,f_+(x))$ for $t>T$; (ii) $\tilde f_t$ is $C^\infty$-close to $f_t$; (iii) the double points of $G$ are in one-to-one index preserving correspondence with the double points of the regular homotopy $f_t$.

hypotheses.text: Y is a contact manifold with a chosen contact form alpha (xi = ker alpha); the target is its symplectization R x Y with form d(e^s alpha).
f_t: Lambda -> Y, t in [-1,1], is a self-transverse regular Legendrian homotopy (the immersion (x,t) -> (f_t(x),t) has transverse double points).
The homotopy is constant near its endpoints and its endpoints f_- = f_{-1}, f_+ = f_1 are Legendrian embeddings.

sign.text: The index of a double point is the Whitney intersection sign; for a regular homotopy h_t it is computed from the immersion H(x,t)=(h_t(x),t) into Y x [0,1], and for n even and Lambda orientable I({h_t}) = -I({h_{1-t}}), so the direction of the homotopy matters (mod 2 count if n odd or Lambda non-orientable).

normalization.text: The symplectization of (Y, alpha) is R x Y with symplectic form d(e^s alpha), s the coordinate on the R-factor, and the first component of G is the R-coordinate.

dimension.text: Y has dimension 2n-1 and Lambda dimension n-1 (paper-wide notation).

written.notes: Numbering checked against arXiv:1303.0588v2: theorem-like environments share one counter per section; Section 3 contains Lemma 3.1 (lm:Leg-Lag, embedded version), Lemma 3.2 (lm:Leg-Lag-imm), Lemma 3.3 (lm:compensation), Lemma 3.4 (lm:near-cone). The lemma itself does not restate a dimension bound; the n>2 assumption in Section 2 is attached to the loose-Legendrian subsection only. The proof reduces to one double point and is given in the paper (not cited externally); the embedded case is attributed to Eliashberg-Gromov, Lemma 4.2.5.
written.typing_notes: double_point_index: index of a double point is the Whitney intersection sign; homotopy_immersion: index of a regular homotopy h_t computed from H(x,t)=(h_t(x),t); homotopy_direction: the lemma uses f_t run from f_- (t=-1) to f_+ (t=1), forward; index_group: signed count in Z for n even and Lambda orientable, Z_2 otherwise; reverse_homotopy_index_factor: I({h_{1-t}}) = -1 * I({h_t}), stated for n even (Lambda orientable); symplectization_form: R x Y with d(e^s alpha); r_coordinate: the first component of G is the R-coordinate s; t_vs_s: the homotopy parameter t increases with the R-coordinate s (G(t,x)=(t,f_-(x)) for t<-T, (t,f_+(x)) for t>T); dim_y / dim_lambda: dim Y = 2n-1, dim Lambda = n-1.

entry.statement: Let $h\colon\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^{2n}_{st}$ be a Lagrangian cone over a Legendrian link $\phi\colon S^{n-1}\to S^{2n-1}_{st}$. Then there exists a Hamiltonian regular homotopy $h_t\colon\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^{2n}_{st}$, $t\in[0,1]$, with $h_0=h$, fixed near the singularity and outside a ball $B_R\subset\mathbb R^n$ of some radius $R>0$ centered at $0$, such that: (1) $h_1$ coincides with the cone over a loose Legendrian knot $\tilde\phi$ near $\partial B_{R/2}$; (2) the immersion $h_1^-:=h_1|_{h_1^{-1}(B_{R/2})}$ has exactly one transverse self-intersection point; (3) if $n=2k$ then, for any $\phi$, one can arrange $I(h_1^-)=(-1)^{k-1}$, and if in addition $\phi$ is loose, one can also arrange $I(h_1^-)=(-1)^k$. (Remark 3.5: by scaling, $R$ can be made arbitrarily small.)

hypotheses.text: h is a Lagrangian cone: h^{-1}(0)=0 and h(r,x)=(c r^2, phi(x)) in polar coordinates, with phi: S^{n-1} -> S^{2n-1}_st a Legendrian embedding (the link) and c>0.
Ambient: R^{2n}_st with omega_st = sum dx_i ^ dy_i and Liouville form lambda_st = (1/2) sum (x_j dy_j - y_j dx_j); S^{2n-1}_st carries the contact form given by restricting lambda_st.
Looseness of Legendrian knots is used in the sense of Section 2, set up for contact (2n-1)-manifolds with n>2.
For the sign statement (3): n is even, n=2k.
For the option I(h_1^-) = (-1)^k: the link phi is itself a loose Legendrian knot.

variables.n: dimension of the Lagrangian (cone R^n in R^{2n})
variables.c: positive constant in the Lagrangian cone h(r,x)=(c r^2, phi(x))

sign.text: I(f) is the Whitney self-intersection number: for n even and L orientable the algebraic count of double points with intersection signs in the oriented target (sign of (df(T_{p0}L), df(T_{p1}L)) against the orientation of the ambient space), otherwise the mod 2 count; for an immersion with a conical point it is computed away from the conical point.

normalization.text: omega_st = sum dx_i ^ dy_i on R^{2n}; contact form alpha_st on S^{2n-1} is the restriction of lambda_st = (1/2) sum (x_j dy_j - y_j dx_j); omega_st = d(r^2 alpha_st) in polar coordinates, and cones are h(r,x)=(c r^2, phi(x)).

hamiltonian.text: A Lagrangian regular homotopy f_t is Hamiltonian if the class [iota_{d/dt} F^* omega |_{L x t}] in H^1(L) is independent of t.

written.notes: Numbering checked against arXiv:1303.0588v2 (Lemma 3.1 lm:Leg-Lag, 3.2 lm:Leg-Lag-imm, 3.3 lm:compensation, 3.4 lm:near-cone, Remark 3.5). The two sign alternatives in (3) are exactly (-1)^{k-1} for arbitrary phi and (-1)^k additionally available when phi is loose; for odd n no sign statement is made. The paper writes 'n>2' explicitly in Section 2.2 (loose Legendrian submanifolds); the lemma statement itself does not repeat it.
written.typing_notes: k: half the dimension, n = 2k (n >= 3 so k >= 2; n <= 40). I_arbitrary_link: Whitney self-intersection number I(h_1^-) achievable for any Legendrian link phi. I_loose_link: the alternative value achievable when phi is loose. self_intersection_count: algebraic (signed, n even, L orientable) vs mod2 count. intersection_sign_reference: double-point sign compares (df(T_p0 L), df(T_p1 L)) with the orientation of the ambient R^{2n}. branch_order: which preimage's tangent plane comes first in the sign comparison. conical_point: whether the conical point is counted (excluded = computed away from it). symplectic_form: omega_st = sum dx_i ^ dy_i. liouville_form: lambda_st = (1/2) sum (x dy - y dx). contact_form: alpha_st is the restriction of lambda_st to S^{2n-1}. cone_radial_power: exponent of r in cone h(r,x) = (c r^power, phi(x)). hamiltonian_condition: regular homotopy is Hamiltonian iff the flux class in H^1(L) is t-independent. Case sign_option is the user's pick between the two achievable values, not a convention.
written.case_notes: Hypothesis 4 (n=2k) is scoped to statement (3), but both sign_option cases live inside (3), so it is needed whatever sign option is used; tagged general ({}). Equivalent to listing both sign_option cases.

entry.statement: Lemma 3.15 (Separation). Assume (h), (D) and (S). Let p<1. There is some constant c=c(p,\bar\Lambda)>0 such that if R>1/c and v_0 \notin \mathfrak B_{6R} \subset D, then P[ Q(\Phi_{3R}) \wedge Q(\Theta_{2R}) > c | \Theta_R, \Phi_{4R}, Z ] > p, provided that P[Z | \Theta_R, \Phi_{4R}] > 0. Here \Phi_R=(D,\partial_+,h_\partial,v_0,ext_R\gamma,ext_R S) is the outer configuration, \Theta_R=(\beta_R^s, int_R \bar S) the inner configuration, Z = {S_\tau = 0} \cap {e^*_s \subset \gamma} (\tau the first time the walk S hits \partial D(\gamma)), and Q is the 'quality' (separation of strands, normalized by R and capped at 1/100; set to 0 in degenerate cases) defined just before Lemma 3.14.

hypotheses.text: (h): D is a bounded domain of R^2 whose boundary is a subgraph of the triangular lattice T; h is the DGFF on D with boundary values h_\partial on V_\partial satisfying ||h_\partial||_\infty <= \bar\Lambda for a fixed constant \bar\Lambda>0.

(D): D is simply connected, \partial D is a simple closed curve, with two distinct marked midpoints of T-edges x_\partial, y_\partial on \partial D splitting it into arcs \partial_+ (counterclockwise from x_\partial to y_\partial) and \partial_-.

(S): \gamma is the zero-height interface of h from x_\partial to y_\partial; v_0 is a T-vertex in D; S is a simple random walk on T started at v_0, independent of h; \tau is the first time S hits \partial D(\gamma).
p < 1 (the constant c depends on p and \bar\Lambda).
v_0 \notin \mathfrak B_{6R} and \mathfrak B_{6R} \subset D, where \mathfrak B_r is the union of hexagons of the dual hexagonal grid meeting the ball B(0,r).
phrases: ball of radius 6r contained in d

hypotheses.text: P[Z | \Theta_R, \Phi_{4R}] > 0 (non-degenerate conditioning).

variables.R: scale (radius) of the ball around the origin
variables.c: constant c(p, \bar\Lambda) > 0 provided by the lemma

normalization.text: DGFF density proportional to exp(-sum_{edges {u,v}} (h(v)-h(u))^2/2) on the triangular lattice with unit edge length.

sign.text: Interfaces are oriented so that the positive region D^+ is on their right (clockwise around D^+); \partial_+ is the counterclockwise arc from x_\partial to y_\partial, and e^*_s is oriented consistently with the arc of \beta from \hat x to \hat y.

indexing.text: Numbering as in arXiv:math/0605337v3: Lemma 3.15 is the Separation Lemma (label l.separation) in Section 3.5 'Meeting of random walk and interface'.

written.notes: Numbering computed from the shared theorem counter within Section 3 of the v3 LaTeX source (3.13 = l.aleq, 3.14 = Compatibility, 3.15 = Separation). The quality functional Q and configurations \Phi_R, \Theta_R depend on the setup of Section 3.5 (origin as the special point, edges e_s, \beta = component of the interface through e^*_s inside \mathfrak B_R).

entry.statement: Lemma 3.24. Assume (h) and (D). There are constants c>0, \alpha_3>0, both depending only on \bar\Lambda, such that for every \delta>0, P[ dist(v_0, \gamma) < \delta dist(v_0, \partial D) ] < c \delta^{\alpha_3}, where \gamma is the zero-height interface of the DGFF h from x_\partial to y_\partial and v_0 is a vertex of D.

hypotheses.text: (h): D is a bounded domain of R^2 whose boundary is a subgraph of the triangular lattice T; h is the DGFF on D with boundary values h_\partial satisfying ||h_\partial||_\infty <= \bar\Lambda for a fixed \bar\Lambda>0.

(D): D is simply connected with \partial D a simple closed curve, and two marked distinct midpoints of T-edges x_\partial, y_\partial on \partial D; \gamma is the interface from x_\partial to y_\partial.
v_0 is a vertex of T in D (the point from setup (S); the random walk itself plays no role in this lemma, and assumption (\partial) on the boundary signs is not required).
\delta > 0 arbitrary.

variables.delta: ratio of the distance threshold to dist(v_0, \partial D)

normalization.text: DGFF density proportional to exp(-sum_{edges {u,v}} (h(v)-h(u))^2/2) on the triangular lattice with unit edge length.

indexing.text: Numbering as in arXiv:math/0605337v3: Lemma 3.24 is label l.farvv in Section 3.7 'Boundary values of the interface'.

written.notes: Only (h) and (D) are assumed (unlike the neighbouring Lemma 3.23 and Proposition 3.25, which also assume (S) and (\partial)). The constants depend only on \bar\Lambda (uniform in D, h_\partial, v_0). The authors remark they expect the bound \delta^{1/2+o(1)}.
written.typing_notes: dgff_energy_factor: coefficient of sum (h(v)-h(u))^2 in the exponent of the DGFF density (half = exp(-sum/2)). lattice: underlying lattice of the field. edge_length: lattice edge length.

entry.statement: ([DHP, Remark 2.6] and [GL, Theorem 4.3].) Let $(X,\Delta)$ be a projective klt pair such that $\Delta$ is a $\mathbb Q$-divisor. Then $(X,\Delta)$ has a good minimal model if and only if $\kappa_\sigma(X,K_X+\Delta)=\kappa(X,K_X+\Delta)$.

hypotheses.text: $(X,\Delta)$ is a projective klt pair over $\mathbb C$.
$\Delta$ is a $\mathbb Q$-divisor.

numerical_dimension.text: kappa_sigma is Nakayama's numerical Kodaira dimension (as in Nakayama, Zariski-decomposition and abundance), which by Lesieutre's example can differ from kappa_nu.

ground_field.text: Works over the complex number field C throughout.

written.notes: The theorem is quoted from DHP and Gongyo-Lehmann; the corrigendum explains that its proof only needs the weaker inequality (3.3) kappa_sigma(D+f^*Q) >= kappa_sigma(D;X/Y)+kappa(Q) in place of Nakayama's (3.1). The arXiv source was read in place of the J-STAGE/author PDF; the bibliography gives no arXiv version, and the latest arXiv version is titled as the corrigendum.
written.typing_notes: kappa_sigma: numerical Kodaira dimension in Nakayama's sense (not kappa_nu, which can differ); ground_field: varieties over C.

entry.statement: Lemma 19.1 (Log-linear bound on rectangle crossing counts). There exists a constant c_lin in (0,1) (independent of c in [1,2]) such that for any n in Z_{>=0} and any rectangle R := [[w x \rho w]] + u, with w >= 1, \rho >= 1, u in R^2, \mu_{Z^2}[ #AltHor^{\bar\omega}(R) >= 2n | E ] <= (1 - c_lin^{\rho})^n, where E is any event measurable in terms of the even spins and edges at \ell^\infty-distance at least w/5 from R. Moreover the same bounds hold with \mu_{Z^2} replaced by \mu_{Cyl_L}, provided 2(\rho+1/5)w <= L, with R regarded as a rectangle on the cylinder. Analogous bounds hold for vertical crossings, in the plane and on the cylinder. Here #AltHor^{\bar\omega}(R) is the maximal 2k such that \bar\omega=(\omega^+,\omega^-) has 2k alternating (\omega^+,\omega^-,...) left-right crossings of R.

hypotheses.text: Six-vertex model with a=b=1 and c in [1,2] (Delta = 1 - c^2/2), studied through its spin representation; \mu_{Z^2} is the full-plane spin measure (Theorem 17.1), \mu_{Cyl_L} the cylinder spin measure; \bar\omega=(\omega^+,\omega^-) the induced percolations on the even sublattice.
n is a nonnegative integer.
R = [[w x \rho w]] + u is a rectangle with w >= 1 and aspect parameter \rho >= 1, u in R^2.
The conditioning event E is measurable with respect to even spins and edges at \ell^\infty-distance at least w/5 from R (macroscopic buffer zone).
phrases: measurable in terms of the even spins

hypotheses.text: For the cylinder version: 2(\rho + 1/5) w <= L, where Cyl_L = Z x (Z/LZ) with L even.

variables.n: half the number of alternating crossings

normalization.text: Six-vertex weights a=b=1, c in [1,2]; Delta = (a^2+b^2-c^2)/(2ab).

indexing.text: Numbering as in arXiv:2603.06268v1, Section 19 'Bounds on crossing counts'; c_lin is the constant named in this lemma.

crossings.text: Alternating horizontal crossings counted as the largest even number 2k of vertices s_1^+,s_1^-,...,s_k^+,s_k^- in descending order on the left side, each connected to the right side within R by \omega^+ resp. \omega^-.

written.notes: The notation [[w x \rho w]] is not defined in the source text; from the cylinder condition it appears that \rho w is the side length in the cylinder's periodic direction, but this is an inference. The lemma is immediately followed by Remark 19.3 giving \mu_{Z^2}[#AltHor | E] <= 2 c_lin^{-\rho}.
written.typing_notes: weight_a, weight_b: six-vertex weights a and b. delta_formula: Delta = (a^2+b^2-c^2)/(2ab). crossing_count_parity: #AltHor counts the largest even number 2k. alternation_start: which percolation (omega^+ = plus) carries the first crossing. crossing_direction: horizontal crossings join left side to right side. left_side_order: order of the starting vertices s_1^+, s_1^-, ... along the left side.

entry.statement: Lemma 19.4 (Partial circuit estimate). Fix r in [4,\infty) and x in R^2. Let (D_i)_i be a finite family of even domains, B the set of edges in \cup_i \partial D_i contained in the box \Lambda_{2r}(x)=[-2r,2r]^2+x, and U := \cup_i E_even(D_i). Then for any event E measurable in terms of the even spins and edges contained in U and such that \mu_{Z^2}[E \cap {B \subset \omega^-}] > 0, \mu_{Z^2}[ Circuit^{\omega^- \cup U}(A_{2r,r}(x)) | E \cap {B \subset \omega^-} ] >= c_circuit, where A_{2r,r}(x) = \Lambda_{2r}(x) \setminus \Lambda_r(x) and Circuit^S(A) is the event that S \cap A contains a non-contractible circuit of the annulus A; c_circuit > 0 is the constant of the Circuit estimate (Theorem 16.4), independent of c in [1,2].

hypotheses.text: Six-vertex model with a=b=1, c in [1,2], via its spin representation; \mu_{Z^2} is the full-plane spin measure; \omega^- is the percolation of the even sublattice connecting minus spins.
r >= 4 and x in R^2.
(D_i)_i is a finite family of even domains (domains bounded by a self-avoiding circuit of the even sublattice).
E is measurable with respect to even spins and edges contained in U = \cup_i E_even(D_i).
phrases: measurable in terms of the even spins and edges

hypotheses.text: \mu_{Z^2}[E \cap {B \subset \omega^-}] > 0.

variables.r: inner radius of the annulus A_{2r,r}(x)

normalization.text: Six-vertex weights a=b=1, c in [1,2]; boxes are \ell^\infty boxes \Lambda_n=[-n,n]^2 and annuli A_{R,r}=\Lambda_R\setminus\Lambda_r.

indexing.text: Numbering as in arXiv:2603.06268v1, Section 19 (Lemma 19.1, Remarks 19.2-19.3, Lemma 19.4); c_circuit is the constant of Theorem 16.4 (Circuit estimate).

written.notes: The event is for the set \omega^- \cup U (circuits may use edges of U, the 'scarred' region), not \omega^- alone. The lower bound is the same constant c_circuit as in the Circuit estimate with + boundary conditions.
written.typing_notes: weight_a / weight_b: six-vertex weights a=b=1 (c in [1,2]); box_norm: boxes are l^infinity boxes; box: Lambda_n=[-n,n]^2; annulus: A_{R,r}=Lambda_R minus Lambda_r.

entry.statement: Theorem 1.2. For every fixed x in [1/\sqrt2, 1] there exists \sigma(x) in (0,\infty), independent of D and of the inside approximation of Definition 1.1, such that h_\delta/\sigma(x) => \Phi_D in D'(D). In particular the fields are tight as random distributions and, for every k >= 1 and f_1,...,f_k in C_c^\infty(D), the vector (h_\delta(f_i)/\sigma(x))_{i<=k} converges to (\Phi_D(f_i))_{i<=k}; all mixed moments of these vectors converge. Here h_\delta is the integer Lipschitz height on the faces F_\delta of \delta H (hexagonal lattice) inside the cycle \gamma_\delta, zero on boundary faces, with P(h) proportional to x^{N_\delta(h)}, N_\delta(h) = number of adjacent face pairs with different heights; h_\delta is extended as a constant on each face and paired with test functions by Euclidean area, h_\delta(f)=\int_D h_\delta f dz; \Phi_D is the zero-Dirichlet GFF with covariance G_D = (-\Delta_D)^{-1}.

hypotheses.text: x is fixed in [1/\sqrt2, 1] (edge weight of the loop O(2) model).
D \subset R^2 is a bounded simply connected domain with C^2 Jordan boundary.

Inside approximation (Definition 1.1): for mesh \delta -> 0, \gamma_\delta is a simple cycle in \delta H with interior D_\delta \subset D, every compact subset of D is eventually contained in D_\delta, and there are homeomorphic parametrizations with ||\gamma_\delta - \gamma||_\infty -> 0.
Zero boundary condition: h = 0 on the faces \partial F_\delta adjacent to the boundary cycle; |h(u)-h(v)| <= 1 for adjacent faces.
Test functions f_i in C_c^\infty(D); k >= 1.

variables.x: edge weight per unit height change (loop O(2) edge weight)

normalization.text: GFF covariance E[\Phi_D(f)\Phi_D(g)] = \int\int f G_D g with G_D=(-\Delta_D)^{-1} for the Euclidean Laplacian, so G_D(z,w) ~ (2\pi)^{-1} log(1/|z-w|); h_\delta is not rescaled in amplitude (no logarithmic factor), only divided by \sigma(x).

pairing.text: Euclidean area pairing h_\delta(f)=\sum_u w_{\delta,f}(u) h_\delta(u) with w_{\delta,f}(u)=\int_{face at u} f; lattice \delta H with face centres forming \delta T, T = Z(1,0)+Z(1/2,\sqrt3/2).

fourier.text: \hat f(p)=\int e^{-ip\cdot z} f(z)dz; \sigma(x)=\sqrt v with v=(2\pi)^2 c where c dp/|p|^2 is the limiting spectral measure.

written.notes: Numbering: Definition 1.1 (Inside approximation) then Theorem 1.2 (label thm:main), shared counter within Section 1. The theorem holds for each fixed x; it gives no formula for \sigma(x) and does not claim \sigma is independent of x. Constants elsewhere may depend on x non-uniformly.

entry.statement: Let $(X,\lambda)$ be a simply connected Liouville manifold with a negative end $X_-$, and $f\colon L\to X$ a cylindrical at $-\infty$ exact self-transverse Lagrangian immersion with finitely many self-intersections. Suppose that $I(f)=0$, and the asymptotic negative boundary $\Lambda$ of $f$ has a component which is loose in the complement of the others. If $n=3$ suppose, in addition, that $X\setminus f(L)$ has infinite Gromov width. Then there exists a compactly supported Hamiltonian regular homotopy $f_t$ connecting $f_0=f$ with an embedding $f_1$. (Following remark: if $X$ is not simply connected the statement remains true with $I(f)$ understood as an element of the group ring of $\pi_1(X)$.)

hypotheses.text: (X, lambda) is a simply connected Liouville manifold with a negative (Liouville) end X_-.
f: L -> X is a proper Lagrangian immersion, cylindrical at -infinity (embedding on L_-, sending S to the Liouville field Z).
f is exact: the absolute action class a(f) = [f^* lambda] in H^1(L) vanishes.
f is self-transverse with finitely many self-intersection (double) points.
The self-intersection index vanishes: I(f) = 0 (signed count for n even, L orientable; element of Z_2 otherwise).
The asymptotic negative boundary Lambda of f has a component which is loose in the complement of the other components.
Implicit dimension: loose Legendrians are used in contact manifolds of dimension 2n-1 > 3 (Proposition 2.1), i.e. n >= 3 (Theorem 2.2 states n >= 3 explicitly).
If n = 3: X minus f(L) has infinite Gromov width.
L is a connected n-manifold (needed for the definition of I(f)).

variables.I_f: relative self-intersection index I(f) of the immersion (integer for n even and L orientable, else in Z/2)

sign.text: I(f) (n even, L connected orientable, X oriented) is the signed count of double points, the sign of f(p^0)=f(p^1) being +1 iff the orientation given by (df_{p^0}(L), df_{p^1}(L)) agrees with that of X; for n odd or L non-orientable I(f) is in Z_2.

normalization.text: A negative Liouville end is identified, via the flow of the Liouville field Z with lambda = i(Z) omega and alpha = lambda|_Y, with the negative symplectization ((-infinity,0] x Y, d(t alpha)) as written in the source.

hamiltonian.text: A compactly supported Lagrangian regular homotopy f_t is Hamiltonian if [iota_{d/dt} F^* omega |_{L x t}] in H^1(L) is independent of t; exactness means a(f) = [f^* lambda] = 0 in H^1(L).

entry.statement: (Log Abundance.) Let the pair $(X,\Delta)$ consist of a threefold $X$ and boundary $\Delta$, such that $K_X+\Delta$ is nef and log canonical. Then $|m(K_X+\Delta)|$ is basepoint free for some $m$.

hypotheses.text: $X$ is a threefold (normal variety of dimension 3 over $\mathbb C$); the paper assumes $X$ projective for statements, though (1.1) is proved assuming only $X$ proper (see 7.1).
$\Delta$ is a boundary: a $\mathbb Q$-Weil divisor $\sum d_i\Delta_i$ with $0\le d_i\le 1$.
$K_X+\Delta$ is log canonical (in the sense of (2.1.3) of Kollár et al., Flips and abundance).
$K_X+\Delta$ is nef.

boundary.text: A boundary is a Q-Weil divisor with all coefficients in [0,1] (rational, not real, coefficients); S denotes the coefficient-one part and B the rest.

semiample.text: D is semi-ample if |mD| is base point free for some positive integer m.

entry.statement: If $X$ is a compact normal Kähler variety, $\alpha\in H^{1,1}_{\rm BC}(X)$ is big if $\alpha\ge\omega$ where $\omega$ is a Kähler current; equivalently, $\alpha$ is big if it admits a Kähler current $T$ with $[T]\in\alpha$. If $f:X\to Y$ is a birational morphism of normal varieties, then $f_*\alpha$ is called modified big. Note: $f_*\alpha$ may not be locally exact; however if $f_*\alpha\in H^{1,1}_{\rm BC}(Y)$ and $Y$ is Kähler, then $f_*\alpha$ is big.

hypotheses.text: $X$ is a compact normal Kähler variety and $\alpha\in H^{1,1}_{\rm BC}(X)$ (Bott-Chern class).
For 'modified big': $f:X\to Y$ is a birational morphism of normal varieties and $\alpha$ is big on $X$; the class $f_*\alpha$ on $Y$ is modified big.
For the final remark: $f_*\alpha\in H^{1,1}_{\rm BC}(Y)$ and $Y$ is Kähler, in which case $f_*\alpha$ is big.

bigness.text: Big means containing a Kähler current (alpha >= omega for a Kähler current omega), for classes in Bott-Chern cohomology H^{1,1}_BC.

modified_big.text: Modified big means the pushforward f_* alpha of a big class alpha under a birational morphism f of normal varieties (not necessarily a Bott-Chern class on Y).

written.notes: Definition 2.8 is the first environment of Subsection 'Big classes' (theorem counter, numbered within section 2).
written.typing_notes: big_definition: a class is big iff it contains a Kahler current (alpha >= omega). class_cohomology: classes live in H^{1,1}_BC. modified_big_definition: f_* alpha for big alpha and f birational morphism of normal varieties. modified_big_target_class: whether f_* alpha is required to be a Bott-Chern class on Y (not required).

entry.statement: Let $X$ be a compact Fujiki class $\mathcal C$ variety and $(X,B+\bbeta)$ a generalized pair such that $B+\bbeta_X$ is modified big. Then there is a generalized pair $(X,G+\ggamma)$, a resolution $X'\to X$ and a Kähler form $\omega'$ on $X'$ such that $K_X+B+\bbeta_X\equiv K_X+G+\ggamma_X$, $\ggamma$ descends to $X'$, $\ggamma_{X'}-\omega'$ is nef, and ${\rm NKLT}(X,B+\bbeta)\supset{\rm NKLT}(X,G+\ggamma)$, i.e. $\mathcal J(X,B+\bbeta)\subset\mathcal J(X,G+\ggamma)$. In particular, setting $\ddelta=\ggamma-\bar\omega'$, $(X,G+\ddelta)$ is a generalized pair. If $(X,B+\bbeta)$ is gklt, then so is $(X,G+\ggamma)$.

hypotheses.text: $X$ is a compact variety in Fujiki's class $\mathcal C$.
$(X,B+\bbeta)$ is a generalized pair (in the sense of DHY23, Subsection 2.1).
$B+\bbeta_X$ is modified big (Definition 2.8).
For the last sentence only: $(X,B+\bbeta)$ is gklt.

equivalence.text: $\alpha\equiv\alpha'$ means equality of classes in $H^{1,1}_{\rm BC}(X)$.

multiplier_ideal.text: NKLT and $\mathcal J(X,B+\bbeta)$ are the non-klt locus and multiplier ideal of a generalized pair as defined in Subsection 2.1 of the source (Definition 2.1), which the authors call somewhat non-standard in the singular setting.

entry.statement: Let $f:X\to Z$ be a Moishezon morphism and $X$ a Kähler variety with rational singularities. If there exists an $\mathbb R$-line bundle $L$ such that $L\equiv^{alg}_Z\omega$ for a Kähler form $\omega$ on $X$, that is $L\cdot C=\omega\cdot C$ for all curves $C\subset X$ with $f(C)=$ pt, then $f$ is strongly Moishezon. Moreover, if $X$ is smooth or strongly $\mathbb Q$-factorial klt, then $f$ is projective.

hypotheses.text: $f:X\to Z$ is a Moishezon morphism in the paper's (non-standard) sense of Definition 2.32: a proper morphism for which there is a surjective projective $g:W\to X$ with $f\circ g$ projective. Complex spaces are assumed separated.
$X$ is a Kähler variety with rational singularities.
There is an $\mathbb R$-line bundle $L$ and a Kähler form $\omega$ on $X$ with $L\cdot C=\omega\cdot C$ for every curve $C$ contracted by $f$.
For the 'moreover' part: $X$ is smooth or strongly $\mathbb Q$-factorial klt.

moishezon.text: Moishezon morphism is the non-standard Definition 2.32 (exists surjective projective g: W -> X with f o g projective); strongly Moishezon (X integral) requires g bimeromorphic.

strong_q_factoriality.text: Strongly Q-factorial: every rank-1 reflexive sheaf F has F^{[m]} a line bundle for some m > 0.

written.notes: The proof reduces to the case f a contraction by Stein factorization and uses [CH24, Lemma 2.5] and Lemma 2.40.

entry.statement: Let $f:X\to Z$ be a surjective projective morphism of normal compact Kähler varieties with connected fibers, $(X,B+\bbeta)$ a generalized pair which is gklt over an open subset $U$ of $Z$, such that $B+\bbeta_X$ is modified big and $K_X+B+\bbeta_X\equiv f^*\gamma$ for some $\gamma\in H^{1,1}_{\rm BC}(Z)$. Then $(Z,\DDelta_Z+\ddelta)$ is a generalized pair such that $(U,\DDelta|_U+\ddelta)$ is gklt, i.e. (1) $\DDelta_Z\ge 0$; (2) $\ddelta$ is b-nef (descends to some model $Z'$ with $\ddelta_{Z'}$ nef); (3) the coefficients of components of $\DDelta_{Z'}$ whose images meet $U$ are $<1$ for any birational model $Z'\to Z$. Moreover, possibly after replacing $(X,B+\bbeta)$ by a generalized pair $(X,B'+\bbeta')$ with $K_X+B+\bbeta_X\equiv K_X+B'+\bbeta'_X$ satisfying the same hypotheses, we may assume $\ddelta_Z$ is modified big.

hypotheses.text: $f:X\to Z$ is a surjective projective morphism with connected fibers between normal compact Kähler varieties.
$(X,B+\bbeta)$ is a generalized pair which is gklt over an open subset $U\subset Z$.
$B+\bbeta_X$ is modified big.
$K_X+B+\bbeta_X\equiv f^*\gamma$ for some $\gamma\in H^{1,1}_{\rm BC}(Z)$.

moduli_part.text: If K_X+B+beta_X == f^*gamma, the moduli b-class is delta := bar(gamma) - (K + DDelta), where bar denotes the Cartier closure b-class and K_{Z'} = K_{Z'}.

equivalence.text: $\equiv$ means equality in Bott-Chern cohomology $H^{1,1}_{\rm BC}$.

[Theorem 1.4 states more precisely: there is a Moishezon contraction $f:X\to Y$ with $Y$ a compact Kähler space and $\alpha\equiv f^*\gamma$ for a Kähler class $\gamma$ on $Y$; if $X$ is strongly $\mathbb Q$-factorial, $f$ is projective.]

entry.statement: Theorem 1.2 (Existence of Gibbs measure and delocalisation) for the loop O(2) model on the hexagonal lattice H with edge-weight 1, P_D(\omega) \propto 2^{\ell(\omega)}. (i) For any increasing sequence of domains D_n converging to H, P_{D_n} has a limit P_H. (ii) P_H is supported on even subgraphs of H containing only finite loops. (iii) P_H is ergodic and invariant under translations and rotations by \pi/3. (iv) There exists c>0 such that for any even integer n and any finite domain D containing \Lambda_n, or D=H, P_D(there exists a loop in \Lambda_n surrounding \Lambda_{n/2}) >= c. Moreover there exists \rho<1 such that for any finite domain D, with n = dist(0, \partial_E D), P_D(there exist two loops surrounding \Lambda_{\rho n}) <= 1-c. (v) With N_D the number of loops surrounding 0 contained in D, there are c,C>0 such that for any domain D, c log dist(0,D^c) <= E_D(N_D) <= C log dist(0,D^c); the same holds with E_H(N_D) in place of E_D(N_D); in particular P_H-a.s. infinitely many loops surround the origin.

hypotheses.text: Loop O(2) model on the hexagonal lattice H with edge-weight x=1 (n=2) and empty boundary conditions on a domain D (subgraph bounded by a self-avoiding polygon \partial_E D; loops may not use edges of \partial_E D).
For (i): (D_n) is an increasing sequence of domains converging to H (every \Lambda_k is contained in all but finitely many D_n).

For the first bound of (iv): n is an even integer and D is a finite domain containing \Lambda_n (or D = H); \Lambda_n is the domain bounded by a contour around the faces at graph distance n from 0 in T.
For the second bound of (iv): D finite domain and n = dist(0, \partial_E D); the bound concerns two loops surrounding \Lambda_{\rho n} for some \rho<1 given by the theorem.

variables.n: radius index of the hexagonal ball \Lambda_n (graph distance in T)

normalization.text: Hexagonal lattice embedded with the origin at a face centre and distance 1 between centres of adjacent faces; loop weight 2 per loop and edge weight 1.

indexing.text: Numbering as in arXiv:1810.05592v3: Theorem 1.1 is thm:lipschitz, Theorem 1.2 is thm:loops (label), Theorem 1.3 is uniqueness of the Gibbs measure.

written.notes: The theorem is for edge weight x=1 only (uniform Lipschitz functions). The upper bound in (iv) is for two loops in a narrow annulus, not a single loop; the authors state that a one-loop bound for any \rho<1 is only conjectured.

entry.statement: Proposition 2. Let -a < 0 < b. (1) When a+b < 2\lambda, it is not possible to construct a BTLS A such that h_A \in {-a, b} almost surely. (2) When a+b >= 2\lambda, it is possible to construct a BTLS A_{-a,b} coupled with a GFF \Gamma such that h_A \in {-a,b} almost surely. Moreover the sets A_{-a,b} are: unique (if A' is another BTLS coupled with the same \Gamma such that for all z in D, h_{A'}(z) \in {-a,b} a.s., then A' = A_{-a,b} a.s.); measurable functions of the GFF \Gamma they are coupled with; monotonic: if [a,b] \subset [a',b'] and -a<0<b with a+b >= 2\lambda, then a.s. A_{-a,b} \subset A_{-a',b'}. Here \lambda = \sqrt{\pi/8} and BTLS means bounded-type thin local set (local set with |h_A| <= K, isolated-component condition, and thinness (\Gamma_A,f) = \int_{D\setminus A} h_A f).

entry.statement: (Numerical type of a graph image.) Working at the ordinary point $t=0$ with $Y_\Lambda=E(\mathsf q)^8$ ($E(\mathsf q)$ the Tate elliptic curve over the complete Novikov field $\Lambda$, $H_{Y,a}$ a principal theta line from the $a$th factor): for any finite family-Floer $A_\infty$ construction (finite transverse collection of the ordinary graph branes in the torus fibration $T\to\mathbb R^8_q/\mathbb Z^8$, mapped to twisted analytic perfect complexes on $Y_\Lambda^{an}$, covariant convention), the image of a graph $X=\{p=A_Xq+\nabla f_X(q)\}$ is a line bundle, up to an integer shift. Before fixing the uniform convention sign, its numerical type is $\varepsilon A_X$, with one $\varepsilon\in\{1,-1\}$ for the whole construction. More precisely, it is a shift of $\bigotimes_{a=1}^8 H_{Y,a}^{\varepsilon (A_X)_{aa}}\otimes P_X$ with $P_X\in\mathrm{Pic}^0(Y_\Lambda)$.

hypotheses.text: X is a graph label X = {p = A_X q + grad f_X(q)} in T with A_X = h_0 k 1_8 (k >= 1) or A_X = S_- (diagonal integral symmetric slope matrices) and f_X a smooth periodic real function.

The construction is a finite family Floer A_infinity functor (Abouzaid) on a finite transverse collection of embedded, integer-graded, tautologically unobstructed graph branes with base-frame spin structure, trivial valuation-unitary local system and integer grading continued from constant symmetric graph planes, after a sufficiently fine family cover.

The fibration T -> R^8_q / Z^8 is a closed nonsingular Lagrangian torus fibration; the rigid dual is Y_Lambda^an with Y_Lambda = E(q)^8, E(q) the Tate curve with multiplicative period q over the complete Novikov field.
Work at the ordinary point t=0 (no B-weight imposed) with the covariant convention for the mirror functor; a contravariant family model must first be composed with perfect duality.

entry.statement: Lemma 7.3 (Cusp base change on the canonical branch; label lem:cusp-base-change). An ordinary section modulo $p^M$ on the canonical branch whose constant terms vanish, extended by zero on the other branches, is a section of $\mathcal M_\lambda/p^M$ over the ordinary open. The assertion remains true with coefficients in $\mathcal O[t]/(p^M,t^b)$ and after finite extension of coefficients. Here $\mathcal M_\lambda=(Y^{tor}\to X^{\min})_*(\mathcal E_\lambda(-\pi^*D))$, $\pi:Y^{tor}\to X^{tor}$ is the finite normalization in the generic-fiber level $J$, $D$ the reduced toroidal boundary of $X^{tor}$, and $\mathcal E_\lambda$ is built at each distinguished embedding from $(\det\omega^+)^{\lambda_3}\otimes\mathcal D_d(\omega^+)$, $\mathcal D_d(\mathcal H)=(\mathrm{Sym}^d((\wedge^2\mathcal H)^\vee))^\vee$, $d=m-1$, and the opposite differential line to exponent $-\lambda_4$; the canonical branch is the open and closed branch of Lemma 7.1 on which the rank-three flag equals the multiplicative subgroup.

hypotheses.text: Ordinary refers to the integral PEL variety for the target unitary group; its integral datum is hyperspecial and totally split at p (section 7 standing assumption; no reduction condition on A_0).

A neat tame base level is chosen; the depth s of the p-level is fixed; k is enlarged once to contain the required p^s-th roots of unity with compatible cyclotomic frames; all models are after this base extension.

X^tor and X^min are compatible hyperspecial integral toroidal and minimal compactifications (good-prime PEL constructions of Lan 2013); Y^tor is the finite normalization of X^tor in the generic-fiber level J with the upper (2,1,1) block structure, at distinguished p-adic factors where the ordinary p-divisible group has multiplicative height three and etale height one.
The section lives on the canonical branch (Lemma 7.1) and its constant terms vanish (it is a cusp section modulo p^M); it is extended by zero on the other branches.
Weights: d = m - 1 with weight (m,m,1;-1) at each real place for the theta sections; b = b_*, O_b = O[t]/(t^b); v_p(p) = 1.

entry.statement: If the hypothesis of Theorem 1.2 holds in the required polarized components in every degree, then (1.2) holds for every projective K3 surface. That is: assume that for every $d$ and every component of the moduli space of primitively amply polarized K3 surfaces of degree $2d$, condition (i) [an abelian variety $B$ and $\alpha\in CH^2(S\times B)_{\mathbb Q}$ with $\alpha_*\colon V\to H^2(B,\mathbb Q)$ nonzero, $V=h^\perp$] or condition (ii) [a smooth connected projective surface $Y$ and a dominant generically finite $f\colon Y\to S$ with $f_*(\mathrm{im}[\wedge^2H^0(Y,\Omega^1_Y)\to H^0(Y,\Omega^2_Y)])\neq0$] of Theorem 1.1 holds very generally. Then every projective K3 surface $S$ admits $\Gamma_S\in CH^2(S\times A_S\times A_S)_{\mathbb Q}$ with $(p_{AA})_*(\mathrm{cl}(\Gamma_S)\cup p_S^*x)=\kappa_S(x)$ for all $x\in T(S)$, where $\kappa_S\colon T\to W_S\otimes W_S\hookrightarrow H^2(A_S\times A_S,\mathbb Q)$ is the prescribed full Kuga-Satake map for all stipulated standard data on $T(S)$.

hypotheses.text: For every degree 2d, in the polarized component(s) containing the surfaces of interest, condition (i) or (ii) of Theorem 1.1 holds very generally (about each point, outside a countable union of proper closed analytic subsets of a full polarized period chart; outside countably many proper algebraic subsets of the moduli component suffices).
Condition (i): there are an abelian variety B and a cycle alpha in CH^2(S x B)_Q such that alpha_*: V -> H^2(B,Q) is nonzero.
Condition (ii): there are a smooth connected projective surface Y and a dominant generically finite morphism f: Y -> S with f_*(image of wedge^2 H^0(Omega^1_Y) in H^0(Omega^2_Y)) nonzero.
S is a projective K3 surface over C (it carries a primitive ample class h with h^2 = 2d > 0).

Standard Kuga-Satake data on T(S) are fixed: a rational quadratic polarization Q of T, the full even Clifford construction, parity identification by right multiplication, a rational weight-one polarization, and an isogenous realization A_S.

entry.statement: Theorem 5.1. Let $X$ be a normal projective $4$-fold and $B$ an effective $\mathbb Q$-divisor such that $(X,B)$ is canonical and $\lfloor B\rfloor=0$. Consider a sequence of log flips starting from $(X,B)=(X_0,B_0)$: $(X_0,B_0)\dashrightarrow(X_1,B_1)\dashrightarrow(X_2,B_2)\dashrightarrow\cdots$ over $Z_0, Z_1,\dots$, where $\phi_i:X_i\to Z_i$ is a contraction and $\phi_i^+:X_i^+=X_{i+1}\to Z_i$ is the log flip. Then this sequence terminates after finitely many steps.

hypotheses.text: X is a normal projective variety of dimension 4.
B is an effective Q-divisor and (X,B) is canonical.
The round-down of B is zero (automatic if (X,B) is terminal).
The sequence consists of log flips of (X_i,B_i): phi_i: X_i -> Z_i a (flipping) contraction and X_{i+1} the log flip over Z_i.

Theorem 5.2 removes the round-down condition under Q-factoriality and relative Picard number one. Q-factoriality and rho(X_i/Z_i)=1 are NOT assumed in 5.1. entry.statement: Let $X$ be a compact complex variety of Fujiki class $\mathcal C$ and dimension $2n$ with rational singularities, and $\sigma\in H^{2,0}(X)$ the class of a holomorphic 2-form on $X^{reg}$, with $q_{X,\sigma}(\alpha)=\frac n2\int_X(\sigma\bar\sigma)^{n-1}\alpha^2+(1-n)\int_X\sigma^n\bar\sigma^{n-1}\alpha\int_X\sigma^{n-1}\bar\sigma^n\alpha$ (Definition 5.2). Then the quadratic form $q_{X,\sigma}\colon H^2(X,\mathbb R)\otimes H^2(X,\mathbb R)\to\mathbb R(-2)$ is a morphism of $\mathbb R$-Hodge structures. If $X$ is a primitive symplectic variety, $q_{X,\sigma}$ is nondegenerate and has signature $(3,b_2(X)-3)$. Furthermore, if $\sigma$ is chosen such that $\int_X(\sigma\bar\sigma)^n=1$, then $q_{X,\sigma}$ does not depend on $\sigma$.

hypotheses.text: X is a compact complex variety of Fujiki class C with rational singularities, of (complex) dimension 2n.
sigma in H^{2,0}(X) is the cohomology class of a holomorphic 2-form on the regular locus X^reg (the Hodge structure on H^2(X,Z) is pure by Lemma 2.1).

For nondegeneracy and signature: X is a primitive symplectic variety (normal compact Kaehler, H^1(X,O_X)=0, H^0(X^reg,Omega^2)=C sigma, sigma symplectic on X^reg and extending holomorphically to a resolution).
For independence of sigma: sigma is normalized so that int_X (sigma sigma-bar)^n = 1.
